title: Andrew Glasgow of [Corsoun?], Calder Cleir: later holding and locality follow-up
question: Can a later primary rental, tack, deed or parish record identify Elizat Stevinsoun or Robert Glasgow as successor to Andrew Glasgow's holding, and can the testament locality safely be equated with Corstoun/Costoun?
conclusion: No later record located in this bounded pass names Andrew's widow Elizat, his proved son Robert, or a succession from Andrew. The NRS catalogue confirms a Calder Cleir estate geography and identifies the relevant Calder estate series, but its catalogue descriptions do not name the family. A distinct Costoun rental is first catalogued for 1663-1695 (including 1674), too late and not shown to be Andrew's locality. The 1641 apprenticeship identifies James as son of a Robert Glasgow serving at Wester Duddingston, but provides no Andrew, Elizat, Corsoun/Corstoun, Calder Cleir, land, or succession bridge; it cannot identify that Robert as Andrew's son.

findings.claim: Calder Cleir was a named commonty in the Kirknewton/East Calder area and is related in the NRS catalogue to the Morton papers (GD150).
findings.basis: NRS catalogue descriptions for the 1806 and 1839 plans call the subject Calder Cleir/Calderclear commonty and place it at Kirknewton, Midlothian; both list GD150 as related material. This establishes a geographic research corridor, not Andrew's exact farm or tenure.
findings.source_reference: National Records of Scotland, RHP523, Plan of the commonty of Calder Cleir, Kirknewton, Midlothian, 1806; catalogue, open access to catalogue description; digital image only in NRS Virtual Volumes/ScotlandsPeople. Corroborating catalogue item: RHP93287, Plan of Calderclear (Calder Cleir) commonty, Kirknewton, [1839], open catalogue description.

findings.claim: The highest-value unexamined primary series remains the Morton estate material for the Barony of Caldercleir.
findings.basis: The NRS catalogue assigns GD150/696-757 to the Barony of Caldercleir, 1506-1824, and GD150/320-493 to general deeds, 1551-1597. Catalogue-level access is open, but no digitised item image or person-level description naming Andrew, Elizat or Robert was found in this pass.
findings.source_reference: National Records of Scotland, GD150, Papers of the Earls of Morton; catalogue record, access status Open, location Off site. The catalogue is a finding aid, not the underlying rentals/tacks/deeds.

findings.claim: Costoun/Couston cannot presently be substituted for the manuscript [Corsoun?]/printed Corstoun locality.
findings.basis: GD119/450 is catalogued as accounts relating to Costoun, including a rental for 1674, with date range 1663-1695. It supplies neither Andrew Glasgow, Elizat Stevinsoun nor Robert Glasgow, and its date is at least 65 years after Andrew's 1598 confirmation. The catalogue does not equate Costoun with Corsoun/Corstoun in Andrew's testament.
findings.source_reference: National Records of Scotland, GD119/450, Accounts relating to lands of Costoun, including a rental for 1674, intromitted with by Mary Eastone, lady Costoune, 1663-1695; catalogue description, access level not stated in the browse-tree result. A later archival lead only, not evidence of identity or place equivalence.

findings.claim: Robert Glasgow of Wester Duddingston remains a distinct, unbridged candidate rather than Andrew and Elizat's proved son.
findings.basis: The published Edinburgh apprenticeship register records on 16 June 1641 James Glasgow, son of Robert Glasgow, servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston, apprenticed to William Sclaitter, weaver. This proves a father-son statement for James and that Robert's service/residence description, but does not name Andrew, Elizat, Calder Cleir, Corsoun/Corstoun, or an inherited holding. It therefore does not discriminate Robert Glasgow-1156 as Andrew's son.
findings.source_reference: Francis J. Grant, ed., Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583-1666 (Scottish Record Society, 1906), p. 71; public digitised printed transcription, not the original apprenticeship entry.

searches.target: NRS catalogue and web indexes: GD150, Caldercleir, Andrew/Robert Glasgow
searches.result: Confirmed GD150/696-757 as Barony of Caldercleir, 1506-1824, and GD150/320-493 as 1551-1597 deeds; no catalogue-described item naming Andrew, Elizat or Robert. Underlying material requires item-level archive consultation.

searches.target: NRS catalogue and web indexes: Corsoun, Corstoun, Costoun/Couston with Glasgow
searches.result: No person-level Andrew/Elizat/Robert hit. GD119/450 surfaced as later Costoun accounts/rental, but the description supplies no place equivalence or Glasgow name.
RHP523 and RHP93287 confirm the Calder Cleir/Calderclear commonty in the Kirknewton/East Calder area and related GD150 provenance; they do not locate Andrew's holding.

searches.target: Published Edinburgh apprentices: James son of Robert Glasgow, Wester Duddingston, 1641
searches.result: The published entry is real and directly identifies James's father Robert, but has no Andrew/Elizat/Calder or holding reference; it leaves the proposed bridge unproved.

searches.target: Exact web searches for Andrew Glasgow + Costoun and Robert Glasgow + Costoun
searches.result: No relevant early-Lothian primary or derivative record found; results were later/unrelated same-name material.

next_record: Consult NRS GD150/696-757 for rentals, tacks, tenant lists and transfers dated c.1597-1635, then GD150/494-533 and GD150/2027-2060 for a Robert succeeding Andrew or an Elizat/Stevinsoun widow holding the same named land. Capture the exact item reference, folio/image, tenure and place spelling before proposing any identification. If the holding proves Costoun/Couston, separately document the explicit record-based equivalence; do not infer it from orthography.
